lyrics:
The talaros, a woven openwork
Holds what’s thought true
Misconstrued as you
And what is not falls through
The weavers never meant to hold
Such weight upon the stakes
Nothing freely escapes
The account of our mistakes

Every choice a new example
Of the flame or just the candle

A tablet scored, a page impressed
A vivid description of what works best
All mostly meaningless
Not subject nor object nor truth disavowed
Unreasonably quiet and silently loud
Of woven edge and borrowed reeds
The talaros serves, then releases
Once holding on, then letting go
Of all the weight it gathers
Better still, to let them go
What’s holding and what’s held
The talaros never failed
You are not what it gathered

style: The experimental post-rock piece launches with pulsing Hammond B3 grooves and gritty, syncopated guitars, Verses explore intricate rhythmic interplay before spiraling into bold organ and guitar solos, Progressive structures introduce wild key changes, leading to a massive chorus, with dense layers and deep baritone vocals riding swelling, evolving textures that intensify to the finish

impression.text: This track offers a powerful blend of modern alternative rock and progressive metal, creating a dynamic, emotionally charged atmosphere that feels both epic and introspective. The energy remains high throughout, driven by a punchy, tight rhythm section, soaring vocal melodies, and rich, distorted guitar riffs. The production quality is exceptionally clean and spacious, allowing the dense layers of synthesizers, heavy guitars, and expressive vocals to coexist harmoniously without sounding cluttered. A standout feature is the smooth transition from the dramatic synth-infused intro to the hard-hitting rock groove, showcasing the track's excellent dynamic range.

review.review_text: Rose builds this one on a 3/4 pulse at a brisk clip, which is the first surprise: a waltz that never asks you to sway, driven instead by a Hammond groove and gritty guitar working against the meter rather than settling into it. The lyric is the thorniest he's written since the abstractions of 'Prepositions,' turning a Greek word for a woven basket into a meditation on what we hold and what we let fall through, and when the chorus lands on 'Unreasonably quiet and silently loud,' the paradox pays off in the arrangement itself, dense and swelling one moment, spacious the next. His deep baritone rides the middle of it comfortably, and the instrumental stretch around the four-minute mark, that spiral into organ and guitar before the final chorus returns, gives the five-plus minutes room to breathe rather than sprawl. It asks more of a listener than 'Them Bones' did, and the payoff comes on the second or third pass rather than the first: a grower, but a rewarding one for those willing to sit with it.
